paragraphs: This list is for self-questioning only and does not constitute hiring standards, competency scoring, or law enforcement and compliance evaluation conclusions. This page is written according to the United States O*NET-SOC 33-1012.00 'First-Line Supervisors of Police and Detectives' (the Chinese name on this page is aligned to the official occupational scope as 'Police and Detective First-Line Supervisors', and the body text is developed according to that official occupational scope). This occupation is highly jurisdiction-sensitive: in the United States it belongs to the state and local policing system (sworn officers differ greatly in ranks and unions and local procedures, and employment requires passing a background check and police academy training and licensing and medical examination and psychological evaluation), while mainland China uses the people's police and public security and political-legal system (recruitment and police ranks and police service grades and law enforcement authority follow the People's Police Law and competent authority rules, and do not correspond one-to-one with the United States occupational classification). Before comparing positions or development paths, first verify: the local qualification and oath and licensing and background check requirements, police ranks or grades and promotion channels, law enforcement authority and the authorization boundaries for the use of force, duty and shift and standby and overtime arrangements, and the compliance requirements for cases and evidence and records and information disclosure and personal information protection.

Verify with a paper exercise: you are given a completely fictional police supervisory shift task (the jurisdiction and shift and police staffing, the call response and patrol and handling and preliminary case investigation and report items to be completed on duty, the available personnel and vehicles and equipment and communications and detention facilities, one incident of law enforcement dispute or evidence defect or personnel misconduct or mass incident or public opinion incident, and the scheduling and police assignment, pre-shift briefing, on-site supervision, case and evidence supervision, discipline, and reports that need to be completed), and you are required to write out the shift and police assignment, the sequence and compliance key points for call response and handling and supervision and reports, the key points for handling evidence and persons in custody and property, the handling path and reporting for disputes and complaints and public opinion and discipline, the performance and training and record requirements, the coordination with the procuratorate and courts and superiors and the community and the media, and the records and reports related to scheduling and cases and evidence and discipline and equipment, and to mark which decisions must be made by the police head or the legal affairs or discipline inspection and supervision or the procuratorate and competent authorities, and to make clear that this exercise does not involve any real case or individual.

Signals more worth considering: willingness to lead front-line police forces over the long term and bear law enforcement and safety and public opinion and discipline pressure; the ability to improve the team through scheduling and briefings and case supervision and training; willingness to work in shifts and outdoors and on standby and in high-risk environments. Signals to be cautious about: unwillingness to bear law enforcement disputes and public opinion and personnel misconduct and high-risk handling; difficulty accepting strict discipline and compliance and record requirements; imagining this kind of work as merely enforcing the law personally without having to lead people and manage cases and manage discipline.
This card is a career exploration reference and does not constitute a hiring, competency scoring, law enforcement, or compliance conclusion, nor does it provide legal advice.

First judge whether you are willing to make police supervision a long-term career: it requires leading front-line police forces over the long term, bearing case investigation supervision and discipline and performance and compliance goals, organizing scheduling and on-site supervision according to laws and procedures, and bearing management responsibility for the team's law enforcement conduct; verify this with the paper exercise and the seven-day task on this page.

The work of first-line supervisors of police and detectives unfolds around the cycle of 'scheduling and police assignment and pre-shift briefing — on-site supervision and call response and handling review — case investigation supervision and evidence and record review — performance and training and discipline — community and cross-agency and court coordination — budget and policy and equipment and reports': at the start of a period, prepare work schedules and assign tasks to subordinates, explain police operations to subordinates to assist them in performing their duties, and inform personnel about changes in regulations and policies, the impact of new or revised laws, and new techniques in police work; in daily supervision, supervise and coordinate the investigation of criminal cases, provide guidance and professional opinions to investigators and ensure that procedures are conducted in accordance with laws and regulations, read and review subordinates' reports to ensure they meet legal standards and contain no errors, and review the content of written orders to ensure compliance with legal requirements; in the handling and compliance stage, direct the collection, preparation, and handling of evidence and the personal property of persons in custody, inspect facilities and supplies and vehicles and equipment to ensure compliance with standards, conduct spot checks as necessary and order the detention of witnesses and suspects for questioning, and direct the release or transfer of persons in custody; carry out personnel and discipline management, investigate and resolve personnel problems within the organization and allegations of misconduct by employees, monitor and evaluate the work performance of subordinates and approve promotions and transfers, impose disciplinary action on employees who violate departmental rules, and train employees in proper police procedures; carry out external and cross-agency coordination, cooperate with court personnel and officials of other law enforcement agencies as necessary and testify in court, meet with citizens and educational and community groups to conduct community programs and activities and discuss law enforcement issues, and prepare press releases and reply to police correspondence; and take on management responsibilities, developing, implementing, and revising departmental policies and procedures, requisitioning and issuing equipment and supplies, preparing budgets and managing departmental expenditures, and maintaining logs and preparing reports and directing the preparation, processing, and maintenance of departmental records. The emphasis differs greatly across positions: patrol and response supervision emphasizes scheduling and on-site and handling compliance, investigation supervision emphasizes cases and evidence and legal standards, community policing supervision emphasizes community relations and prevention and communication, traffic and specialty unit supervision emphasizes special duty and equipment and safety, office and records supervision emphasizes archives and information disclosure and data compliance, and training and inspection supervision emphasizes training and discipline and internal oversight.

entries.answer: This page is written according to the United States O*NET-SOC 33-1012.00 'First-Line Supervisors of Police and Detectives' (the Chinese name on this page is aligned to the official occupational scope as 'Police and Detective First-Line Supervisors'): directly supervise and coordinate the activities of members of a police force. Specifically this includes: supervise and coordinate the investigation of criminal cases, provide guidance and professional opinions to investigators, and ensure that procedures are conducted in accordance with laws and regulations; prepare work schedules and assign tasks to subordinates; direct the collection, preparation, and handling of evidence and the personal property of persons in custody; investigate and resolve personnel problems within the organization and allegations of misconduct by employees; explain police operations to subordinates to assist them in performing their duties; maintain logs, prepare reports, and direct the preparation, processing, and maintenance of departmental records; inform personnel about changes in regulations and policies, the impact of new or revised laws, and new techniques in police work; train employees in proper police procedures; impose disciplinary action on employees who violate departmental rules; monitor and evaluate the work performance of subordinates and approve promotions and transfers; review the content of written orders to ensure compliance with legal requirements; conduct spot checks and order the detention of witnesses and suspects for questioning; cooperate with court personnel and officials of other law enforcement agencies as necessary and testify in court; meet with citizens and educational and community groups to conduct community programs and activities and discuss law enforcement issues; inspect facilities and supplies and vehicles and equipment to ensure compliance with standards; direct the release or transfer of persons in custody; requisition and issue equipment and supplies; develop, implement, and revise departmental policies and procedures; prepare press releases and reply to police correspondence; prepare budgets and manage departmental expenditures; and read and review subordinates' reports to ensure they meet legal standards and contain no errors. Common reported job titles include Captain, Deputy Sheriff, Detective Sergeant, Lieutenant, Patrol Sergeant, Police Chief, and Shift Supervisor.
entries.question: What do first-line supervisors of police and detectives mainly do?

entries.answer: The responsibilities and authority differ: this occupation is a front-line police supervisory position, whose main output is scheduling and police assignment, on-site and handling supervision, case investigation supervision and evidence and record review, and discipline and performance management, and it is usually a sworn officer or people's police officer with command and supervisory authority; police officers and sheriff's patrol officers and detectives and criminal investigators have specific patrol and response and investigative casework as their output and generally do not carry team command responsibilities; transit and railroad police and police identification and records officers and security guards have law enforcement or security prevention in a specific place or specific function as their output, among which security guards hold no public power; first-line supervisors of correctional officers and correctional officers have custody and correctional supervision as their output; private detectives and investigators have civil or commercial investigations as their output and hold no public power. This occupation does not include positions focused on individual casework without supervisory responsibilities, nor does it include non-law-enforcement security and investigation positions.

subject.name: First-Line Supervisors of Police and Detectives
subject.summary: Directly supervise and coordinate the activities of members of a police force: supervise and coordinate the investigation of criminal cases, provide guidance and professional opinions to investigators, and ensure that procedures are conducted in accordance with laws and regulations; prepare work schedules and assign tasks to subordinates; direct the collection, preparation, and handling of evidence and the personal property of persons in custody; investigate and resolve personnel problems within the organization and allegations of misconduct by employees; explain police operations to subordinates to assist them in performing their duties; maintain logs, prepare reports, and direct the preparation, processing, and maintenance of departmental records; inform personnel about changes in regulations and policies, the impact of new or revised laws, and new techniques in police work; train employees in proper police procedures; impose disciplinary action on employees who violate departmental rules; monitor and evaluate the work performance of subordinates and approve promotions and transfers; review the content of written orders to ensure compliance with legal requirements; conduct spot checks and order the detention of witnesses and suspects for questioning; cooperate with court personnel and officials of other law enforcement agencies as necessary and testify in court; meet with citizens and educational and community groups to conduct community programs and activities and discuss law enforcement issues; inspect facilities and supplies and vehicles and equipment to ensure compliance with standards; direct the release or transfer of persons in custody; requisition and issue equipment and supplies; develop, implement, and revise departmental policies and procedures; prepare press releases and reply to police correspondence; prepare budgets and manage departmental expenditures; and read and review subordinates' reports to ensure they meet legal standards and contain no errors.
